alt: Paper 2 Question 2 is worth 8 marks for AO1 and compares only what the sources show about a focus. Question 4 is worth 16 marks for AO3 and compares the writers’ perspectives and the methods that convey them, across the whole of a 19th-century source and a 20th- or 21st-century source.
caption: Question 2 compares what; Question 4 compares what and how.

alt: Perspective, the wider way of seeing shaped by experience, time and values, produces a viewpoint, the position a writer takes, such as “zoos should close”. Attitude is the writer’s feeling, such as admiring or scornful, and tone is how that feeling sounds, such as ironic or urgent.
caption: Perspective produces the viewpoint; tone is how the attitude sounds.

alt: Five kinds of method: vocabulary, grammar, form, structure, and evidence and voice, each with examples. Below, Source A and Source B are paired opening with opening, ending with ending and anecdote with anecdote.
caption: Compare methods of the same kind so the difference is visible.

alt: A table compares the 19th-century and modern sources by audience (one person against thousands of strangers), conventions (long, balanced sentences and formal address treated as choices that shape tone) and assumptions (what one writer takes for granted, the other may question).
caption: Audience, conventions and assumptions turn the time gap into evidence.

alt: Three strips of paragraph blocks. Integrated answers move between Source A and Source B in every paragraph. Alternating blocks put A then B, with each B paragraph linked back to A. Two separate essays describe A, then B, and compare only at the end, which tends to stay in the lower levels.
caption: Keep comparison constant: integrated paragraphs are safest.

alt: A grid compares the two summit extracts. Perspective: reverent awe in Source A against a summit spoiled by the crowd in Source B. Method: silence and the simile “like the folds of some vast garment” against the flat opening “There was a queue at the summit” and the minor sentence “An actual queue”. Ending: looking upward to “the hand that made these heights” against a question about what “we had all come up here to find”.
caption: Each method is paired with one of the same kind and linked to a perspective.

alt: An empty planning grid lists four aspects (overall perspective, tone and voice, use of evidence, endings) down the side and Source A and Source B across the top. Below: compare perspectives, compare methods and refer to both texts; lead with perspective and follow with method; use whereas, in contrast, similarly or unlike rather than also or and.
caption: Fill the grid first, then write paragraphs that compare in every sentence.
